title: Reporting a defect: reproduction, severity, priority and evidence

videos.script: A defect you found and nobody can reproduce is a defect that stays. {{found}} The report is how it leaves your desk and reaches someone who can fix it. That person was not there when it happened. {{stranger}} So the report has to carry everything: the version, the state you started from, the exact steps, what should have happened and what did. {{fields}} This lesson writes one whole report, for a defect boxoffice has carried since 1.0. A word typed into the tickets field answers with a Python traceback. {{traceback}} You shrink the steps to one curl command that anybody can paste and replay. {{curl}} Then you rate it twice. Severity says how much harm it does. Priority says how soon it gets fixed, and somebody else usually decides that. {{rate}} Last comes the evidence: the transcript, the line in the server's log, and a screenshot. {{evidence}} By the end, your report could be read by a developer who has never met you, and they would not need to ask you anything. {{end}}
